note: Hard B, lineage reading: base.json names this recipe's mother, so the declared difference is against that recipe -- not against the framework stock cfg, which would bury this version's own delta in everything its ancestors wrote. Env paths are grouped by who wrote them: the element set that touched the path (several elements can touch one path in sequence), a version-resolved component, or wiring -- the shared wiring reading this recipe's own document. params_version is filtered as identity: it says which recipe this is, and it is what makes the two recipes different at all.

components.commands.why: v3 widens the forward range to 2 m/s: a 1 m/s cap made foot-pad creeping the optimum

components.height_sensing.why: v3 replaces the ground grid scanner with four foot rings (paper S8, one scan per sole)

components.observations.why: v3 splits the single policy group into proprio/extero/priv, so the network reads streams by name

components.terminations.why: v3 narrows base_contact to the base body (v1/v2 contact every body) and adds the tilt gate

components.terrain.why: v3 swaps the v1/v2 frozen generator for the Miki-aligned terrain (stair top 0.55 m + stepping stones)

v3_anti_drag_reward.why: v3's anti-drag pair: feet_air_time replaced by foot_clearance (r_fc), the swing-time reward

v3_ck_clock.why: v3.1 adds the c_k clock: five DR events become c_k-scaled (func + mode), plus the init_ck event and the three c_k-gated reward callables

v3_contact_headroom.why: v3.6.1 raises the collision stack 2**26 -> 2**28 against the contact overflow

v3_speed_curriculum.why: v3 gates the speed range with the staged curriculum (stage 0 is the (-1, 2) window)
